title: Affine torsion cohomology vanishes above the transcendence-degree support bound
statement: Let $L$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $T$ be an affine scheme of finite type over $L$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-scheme], and let $G$ be a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Let $c\geq0$ be an integer and assume that every point $t$ in the support of $G$ [def-kun-support] satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_L\kappa(t)\leq c$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then $H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},G)=0$ for every integer $r>c$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Convert IsTorsionAbelianSheaf to the local-section torsion predicate using isTorsionAbelianSheaf_characterizations. For a geometric point s above a point of residue transcendence degree greater than c, show s^*G=0 by geometric stalk conservativity. Every algebraic-closure point t of Spec Omega gives a geometric point t followed by s of T above that same point; if its stalk were nonzero the support containment would bound its transcendence degree by c, a contradiction. upperStarCompSheafFiberIso identifies the stalks of s^*G with these zero stalks. The source SupportDimension helper residueFieldHomOfOver_eq identifies its residueFieldTrdeg with the scalar structure in pointsOfTrdegLE.

proof.text: Index by the opens U of T whose closed complement has dimension at most c, and use the canonical kernel supportedIn G U with its monomorphism supportedInι. The top open supplies an index. Intersecting two opens gives an upper stage: the helper dim_finite_union_le bounds the union of their closed complements, and supportedIn_factor constructs the kernel inclusions. These proved helpers are imported privately from SupportDimension and SupportedTorsionCohomologyBound. The local-section form exists_covering_supportedIn says that the resulting kernels locally exhaust G; no chosen arbitrary diagram or new data definition is needed.

proof.text: For each U, construct the reduced closed complement Z with its closed immersion i. Affineness of T and i implies affineness of Z. The closed embedding identifies Z with the complement as topological spaces, so its dimension is at most c. Composite i with the structure map is locally of finite type. Apply the source explicit-dimension affine bound hasTorsionCohomologicalDimensionLE_of_isAffine, with the proved field bound hasTorsionCohomologicalDimensionLE_zero_of_isSepClosed. The source bound reuses the declared Sheaf affine theorem through its explicit-dimension variant and handles the empty scheme as well.

proof.text: Exact open restriction kills supportedIn G U, by the proved isZero_upperStar_supportedIn helper. The source closed-support equivalence mem_essImage_lowerStar_of_isZero_upperStar writes it as i_*M. The private isTorsion_of_mono helper proves torsion passes to subobjects directly on sections: on a covering which kills the image section by n, sectionwise injectivity kills the original section by n. Thus the kernel is torsion. Its inverse image under i is torsion by isTorsion_upperStar; the closed-immersion counit and the image isomorphism embed M into that inverse image, so M is torsion too. The affine bound on Z and bijective_edgeMap_of_isFinite imply H^q(T,supportedIn G U)=0 for q>c. A closed immersion is finite by Mathlib instances.

proof.text: Since T is affine, it is qcqs. Apply the proved source H_map_of_directed_of_locally to the canonical kernel inclusions, their directedness and their local exhaustion. Every H^q(T,G) class comes from a stage, whose group is zero by the preceding step; hence H^q(T,G) is a subsingleton. The inequality r>c>=0 represents r by a natural q with q>c. nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso transports the vanishing from Sheaf.H to the stated derived cohomology object, and AddCommGrpCat.isZero_of_subsingleton finishes.
